title: Implement Lower Bound
problemStatement: Return the first index i with a[i] >= x (n if none).
intuition: Lower bound is binary search on the predicate "a[i] >= x", which is False...False,True...True. You are finding the boundary, not a value.

approaches.title: Optimal: boundary binary search
approaches.idea: Keep a candidate answer; shrink hi when the predicate holds.
approaches.dryRun:
a=[1,2,2,3] x=2
mid=1 a=2>=2 ans=1 hi=0
mid=0 a=1<2 lo=1 -> stop, ans=1
approaches.whyWorks: The predicate is monotone, so the first True is a well-defined boundary.

commonMistakes: Confusing lower bound with upper bound
interviewInsight: Lower/upper bound is the reusable primitive; most sorted-array questions are one line once you have it.

related.title: Binary Search to find X in sorted array
